newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares in five day rally, index up 0.65 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares in five day rally, index up 0.65 pct.

text.p: Bombay blue chips closed higher on Wednesday on the back of foreign fund buying, as the market's winning streak remained strong for the fifth straight session.
Bombay's top-30 share index ended 24.85 points, or 0.65 percent, higher at a provisional 3,863.70, off 3,888.73 --the day's highest mark.
Traders said the rally in share prices was led by frontline stocks such as ACC, Hindustan Lever, Colgate, Nestle and Tata Tea, with a few second-tier stocks also taking part.
"The rally has spread to side-counters, but the market looks a bit dangerous now," said Purvesh Shah, chief dealer at Nucleus Securities, a local firm.
Bombay's top 30-share index has jumped 178 points, or five percent in the last five consecutive sessions.
Much of the surge in buying interest has come from foreign funds, analysts said, adding that funds were picking up blue chips despite a long pending delay in an increase in government-set oil prices.
"Funds are keen buyers in their select universe of stocks," said a dealer at a foreign firm. "The price hike has been pushed to the backgound, at least for the time-being."
Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said on Tuesday his United Front coalition's policy-setting steering committee will take a decision on petroleum product prices on June 15.

Analysts said the government must decide soon how to pay the money it owes to oil companies -- a total of 155 billion rupees ($4.33 billion) at the end of March -- for selling subsided petroleum products well below global prices.

Shares of two wheeler maker LML Ltd jumped 3.50 rupees, or 7.4 percent, to 50.50 at the Bombay exchangee on Wednesday after the firm announced improved results for the six months ended March 31, traders said.
LML said late on Tuesday its net surged 111 percent to 172 million rupees in the six months to March 31, from 81.6 million in the previous year.
